AmeriHealth Caritas · AI-in-Engineering · Agent 1 of 2

Every screen of the FRD → STTM agent

A walkthrough of the review app as a user experiences it — from an empty workspace, through selecting an FRD and running the agent, to the human-in-the-loop review and the hand-off back to SharePoint. Captured 2026-08-22 from the local build against a synthetic corpus; no client documents appear anywhere.

  • 19 screens
  • 5 stages of the journey
  • One real model call made for the results screens (~$0.15)
  • Nothing is ever written to SharePoint by the app
SharePointSystem of record. FRDs and approved STTMs live there; the sync reads, the reviewer uploads.
DatabricksUnity Catalog volumes hold the working copies and the pairing index the picker reads.
Automatic codeSync, pairing, grounding, verdicts, re-render — plain code, no AI.
A person decidesGenerate, resolve, apply, download, upload — each an explicit click.

Set up

01

Select FRD — nothing synced yet

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

The app opens on its one surface. With no tenant wired on this backend the blue notice explains that the library cannot be synced from here; the corpus is empty.

What the user does

Wait for the scheduled SharePoint sync, press Sync from SharePoint now… (enabled once a tenant is configured), or Rebuild index… to index whatever the volumes already hold.

02

Rebuild index — confirm step

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Every state-changing control is two-step. The first click explains what will happen (no SharePoint access, no AI calls) and asks to continue.

What the user does

Rebuild now or Cancel. “Sync from SharePoint now…” has the identical shape.

Select

03

Select FRD — the corpus picker

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Stat tiles (FRDs, approved STTMs, mapped pairs, awaiting an STTM) and the first list: FRDs without an STTM, each with a “no STTM yet” badge.

What the user does

Press Generate STTM on an FRD to draft its mapping.

04

Select FRD — already-mapped FRDs and the sync controls

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

FRDs already mapped shows how each was paired (“name match” or an N% content match) and by which workbook. Below: the sync controls and the index / last-synced stamps.

What the user does

Press View STTM to see the approved workbook; use the controls to sync or rebuild.

05

This FRD already has an STTM

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

The approved STTM is presented first — name, size, how it was paired. Nothing is regenerated on selection. An “Open in SharePoint ↗” link appears when the sync recorded one.

What the user does

Download the STTM (.xlsx), or open Regenerate this mapping anyway….

06

Regenerate — confirm step

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Inline confirmation: the full pipeline runs again, the existing STTM is untouched, nothing is written to SharePoint, and the new draft is scored against it.

What the user does

Continue into the billed-run gate, or Cancel.

Run

07

Start a live, billed run?

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

The cost gate: ~1 model call, the estimate, the expected duration, and a reminder that nothing is written to SharePoint. Backend errors render inline in this card.

What the user does

Run it or Cancel.

08

Processing — in progress

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Four stage dots (five in the deployed App, with a link to the Databricks job run) and the live console. Shown here: ingest done, the AI extraction running.

What the user does

Watch, or go back — the run continues.

09

Run failed

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

A failed stage turns its dot red and a Run failed alert names the stage, the exit code and the log path; the console keeps the traceback.

What the user does

← Select FRD to go back.

Captured with a deliberately invalid API key so the model call fails at stage 02 — nothing was billed.

10

Processing — finished

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

All four stages green; the console ends with the render summary.

What the user does

View results.

Review

11

Results — extraction and template decision

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Extraction: feeds, target tables, rules captured, one card per feed. Template decision: which approved pair (if any) drove the layout, with the scored evidence per candidate; freeform is flagged in words.

What the user does

Read top to bottom; every later section refines this.

12

Results — ambiguity gate and human-in-the-loop review

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

The gate strip: detected / auto-confirmed against the data dictionary / awaiting human review, plus the grounding counts and the gated items. Below it, the Human-in-the-loop review panel lists each question as a card: the FRD rule quoted, why it is being asked, the technical detail, and the choices.

What the user does

Pick a candidate or None of these; the rationale box is optional and audit-only.

The two gated questions on this run were added for the screenshot — the synthetic document gated nothing.

13

Human-in-the-loop — a candidate-less question

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

A weak source match has no candidates to pick from, so its answer is free text. Each card saves independently; Apply resolutions & re-render stays disabled until at least one decision is saved.

What the user does

Type the correct reading and Save resolution.

14

Results — verdict, accuracy, rendered STTM and the hand-off

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Pipeline verdict (PASS / PASS_WITH_FLAGS / FAIL, computed in code), Accuracy vs golden STTM (a score only when a reference STTM for this FRD exists — regenerating a mapped FRD fills it), Download workbook (.xlsx), the Next step — yours, not the agent’s note naming the SharePoint folder to upload to, and the per-feed mapping rows.

What the user does

Download, make final edits in Excel, upload to SharePoint yourself. The app publishes nothing.

15

Human-in-the-loop — both questions answered

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Each card shows its saved time and a green resolved badge; the footer reads “All questions answered.” and the apply button is live.

What the user does

Apply resolutions & re-render the STTM.

16

Re-rendering…

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

Stage 04 re-runs with the decisions applied — no model call, nothing billed. In the deployed App this is the render-only job, with a link to its run.

What the user does

Wait a few seconds.

17

Resolutions applied

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

The button returns with “Last applied …”; the sections above and below have refreshed from the re-rendered contract and workbook.

What the user does

Download the updated workbook, or answer anything still open and apply again.

18

Gate strip after the review

127.0.0.1:8020 — FRD to STTM Agent
What you see

“2 resolved by a reviewer” now appears in the grounding line, and the panel reads 2 of 2 gated questions resolved with each card marked resolved.

What the user does

Continue to the download and hand-off below.

Screens that exist but need a tenant or a workspace

These states are built and covered by tests, but cannot be shown from a laptop with no SharePoint tenant and no Databricks workspace:

  • Sync from SharePoint now… enabled, and its Syncing… / Sync failed / Some library files were skipped alerts, with the SharePoint link on each FRD and STTM.
  • The Databricks-mode Processing screen: five stages (SharePoint fetch, ingest, extract, validate, render) and a View job run in Databricks ↗ link; the same link on the sync and on the re-render.
  • Accuracy vs golden STTM filled in — it appears when a mapped FRD is regenerated and scored against its existing workbook.
  • The Open in SharePoint ↗ button on the already-mapped view, present when the sync recorded the file's link.
